title: A Gate-Based Quantum Computing Framework for Codon Optimization
abstract: Codon optimization is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem with important applications in synthetic biology, protein expression, and biotechnology. While quantum annealing has previously been explored for this problem, the application of gate-based quantum algorithms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present a gate-based quantum computing framework for codon optimization by formulating the optimization objective as an Ising Hamiltonian and expressing it in terms of Pauli operators suitable for gate-based quantum processors. The proposed framework is investigated using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), Sampling Variational Quantum Eigensolver (SVQE), and the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), with benchmarking against exact diagonalization, classical optimization, and quantum annealing. Using a three-amino-acid benchmark, the proposed implementations successfully reproduce the exact ground-state solutions while identifying optimized ansatz selections, optimization strategies, initialization schemes, and hardware execution settings that provide reproducible performance on current noisy quantum hardware. Hardware demonstrations are performed on IBM Quantum processors to evaluate the practical implementation of the proposed workflow. As a work in progress, this study establishes a reproducible computational framework for gate-based quantum codon optimization and provides the foundation for future investigations of larger protein sequences as quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance.
summary: This paper develops a gate-based quantum computing framework to solve codon optimization, a key problem in synthetic biology. By mapping the optimization objective to an Ising Hamiltonian, the authors test VQE, SVQE, and QAOA algorithms on a small benchmark. The study successfully demonstrates the feasibility of this workflow, providing a reproducible foundation for tackling larger biological sequences on current quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses codon optimization, a complex combinatorial problem in synthetic biology, by formulating it as a quantum computation challenge.
main_result: The authors successfully established a reproducible, gate-based quantum workflow for codon optimization, demonstrating that VQE, SVQE, and QAOA can recover the complete set of degenerate ground-state solutions on a small benchmark.
method: The optimization problem is mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian expressed in Pauli operators, which is then solved using variational quantum algorithms (VQE, SVQE, QAOA) and benchmarked against classical and quantum annealing methods.
model_or_system: The system is the codon optimization problem, modeled by a Hamiltonian $H = H_f + H_{GC} + H_R + H_P$. The implementation is tested on IBM Quantum processors using a 10-qubit benchmark derived from a three-amino-acid sequence.
key_observables: The ground-state energy of the Hamiltonian, and the sampling probabilities corresponding to the degenerate ground-state manifold.
important_parameters: The benchmark uses a three-amino-acid sequence (Glu–Gly–Pro) resulting in a 10-qubit problem. Algorithm parameters include ansatz depth (reps) and optimization routines (e.g., COBYLA).
main_assumptions: The work is presented as a framework for future scalability, acknowledging that the current benchmark is small and that hardware performance is sensitive to execution settings like measurement shots and error suppression techniques.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the genetic code wheel. Figure 2 shows the energy spectrum and interaction graph for the 10-qubit problem. Tables II and III summarize the performance of SVQE and QAOA on the IBM Quantum backend under various initialization and hardware settings.
paper_structure: The paper first formulates the biological problem into a constrained Ising Hamiltonian. It then details the mapping to Pauli operators suitable for gate-based quantum processors. The methodology involves benchmarking VQE, SVQE, and QAOA against classical and quantum annealing methods on a small benchmark, culminating in hardware demonstrations on the IBM Quantum backend.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum algorithms (VQE, QAOA) to a highly relevant, real-world problem in synthetic biology, providing a concrete, testable quantum computing framework for molecular design.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. The genetic code wheel illustrating the mapping between mRNA codons and amino acids [5]. Codons are read from the center 5′ outward 3′, corresponding to the first, second, and third nucleotide positions. The figure highlights the degeneracy of the genetic code, in which multiple synonymous codons encode the same amino acid.
